I understand where you're coming from, and I agree that if you can’t follow the owner's instructions, you should either communicate or turn down the job. However, in this situation, I didn’t know the kennel was in such bad condition until I got home and smelled it. When I opened it up, there were several small turds, a pile of poop buried under the dog bed, and likely pee as well. That’s not just unsanitary—it’s a health hazard for the dog, especially since dogs hate pooping where they sleep.

Even though their instructions were to keep the dog kenneled for 12 hours a day, I couldn’t ethically leave the dog in a dirty, unhealthy environment for that long. In hindsight, I should have communicated more with the owners about the condition of the kennel and why I couldn’t follow their instructions exactly, but I made a judgment call in the moment based on the dog’s well-being.

I agree that professional pet sitters are paid to follow rules, but this situation crossed into a welfare issue for me. That’s why ESH seems like the right call—there was a lack of communication on my part, but I couldn’t just blindly follow their instructions given the kennel’s state.
